classification.rationale: CreateContainerConfigError indicates a configuration issue preventing container creation during deployment; the missing secret "db-credentials" is a configuration dependency failure that blocks the pod from starting.

diagnosis.root_cause: The container 'app' in Deployment 'api-054b7b' references a Secret named 'db-credentials' to populate the environment variable 'DB_PASSWORD' via secretKeyRef. That Secret does not exist in namespace 'lab-10', causing Kubernetes to refuse to start the container with CreateContainerConfigError. The Deployment has never been healthy (generation 1, 0 ready replicas) so there is no prior image to roll back to.

evidence.value: Deployment does not have minimum availability.

proposal.rationale: A human must create the Secret 'db-credentials' in namespace 'lab-10' with at least a key that maps to the environment variable 'DB_PASSWORD' used by the 'app' container. The exact key name in the Secret (likely 'password' or similar) and its value must be sourced from a secure credential store — they cannot be read from the cluster. Once the Secret exists, Kubernetes will automatically retry container creation without needing a pod restart. Steps: (1) Identify the correct DB password from your secrets manager. (2) Run: kubectl create secret generic db-credentials --from-literal=<key>=<value> -n lab-10 (or apply it via GitOps). (3) Confirm the env var name 'DB_PASSWORD' matches the secretKeyRef.key in the Deployment spec.
proposal.risk: Providing incorrect or placeholder credentials will cause the application to start but fail at runtime when it attempts to connect to the database.
proposal.delivery: Apply as a pull request against /gitops after a human approves it. The agent does not change the cluster.

similar_incidents.title: PM-2026-079: notification-gateway crash loop after a ConfigMap key rename
similar_incidents.fix: Restored the required key SMTP_HOST in the ConfigMap the Deployment loads with envFrom (keeping the new key too) and restarted the Deployment. Clue: exit code 1 with a config error in the previous container log, normal memory and CPU.
similar_incidents.excerpt: The rename was valid YAML and passed review, but nothing checked that the application still found the keys it requires. A second Deployment that used `valueFrom.configMapKeyRef` on the old key failed earlier and louder, with `CreateContainerConfigError: couldn't find key SMTP_HOST in ConfigMap notify/gateway-config`. ## Evidence - Previous container log: `FATAL config: SMTP_HOST is required` then

similar_incidents.title: PM-2026-072: search-indexer rollout stuck on a tag that was never pushed
similar_incidents.fix: Rolled the container image back to the image of the last ReplicaSet revision that was Ready (indexer:2.13.2, revision 41) via a GitOps pull request, then rebuilt and pushed the missing tag before releasing again.
similar_incidents.excerpt: The registry returned `manifest unknown` for the new tag. Kubernetes behaved as designed: `maxUnavailable: 0` kept the old pod running. ## Evidence - Pod events: `Failed to pull image "...indexer:2.14.0": not found`, then `Back-off pulling image`. - Container state: `waiting.reason: ImagePullBackOff`. - ReplicaSet history: revision 41 image `indexer:2.13.2`, ready 1/1; revision 42 image `indexer:2
